items.title: Default prebuilt binary linking fails with `-Zbuild-dir-new-layout`
items.body:
The new cargo build tree layout (Layout v2/`-Zbuild-dir-new-layout`), with completely separate build directories for each dependency, appears to break linking in the `ort-sys` build script:

```
error: failed to run custom build command for `ort-sys v2.0.0-rc.13`

Caused by:
  process didn't exit successfully: `D:\GIT\foo\target\release\build\ort-sys/c28869258fa93f77\out\build_script_main` (exit code: 101)
  --- stdout
  cargo:rustc-check-cfg=cfg(link_error_generic)
  cargo:rustc-check-cfg=cfg(link_error_bad_dist_features)
  cargo:rustc-check-cfg=cfg(pyke)
  cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=ORT_LIB_PATH
  cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=ORT_LIB_LOCATION
  cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=CARGO_NET_OFFLINE
  cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=ORT_SKIP_DOWNLOAD
  cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=ORT_OFFLINE
  [ort-sys] [DEBUG] Using prebuilt binaries
  cargo:rustc-cfg=pyke
  cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=ORT_CUDA_VERSION
  cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=CUDA_HOME
  cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=NV_CUDA_CUDART_VERSION
  [ort-sys] [DEBUG] detected CUDA 13 from nvcc
  [ort-sys] [DEBUG] looking for prebuilt binaries matching feature set: cuda13, tensorrt
  cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=ORT_CXX_STDLIB
  cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=CXXSTDLIB
  cargo:rustc-link-lib=dxguid
  cargo:rustc-link-lib=DXCORE
  cargo:rustc-link-lib=DXGI
  cargo:rustc-link-lib=D3D12
  cargo:rustc-link-lib=DirectML
  cargo:rerun-if-changed=D:\GIT\scrfd\target\release\build\DirectML.dll
  cargo:rerun-if-changed=D:\GIT\scrfd\target\release\build\onnxruntime_providers_cuda.dll
  cargo:rerun-if-changed=D:\GIT\scrfd\target\release\build\onnxruntime_providers_nv_tensorrt_rtx.dll
  cargo:rerun-if-changed=D:\GIT\scrfd\target\release\build\onnxruntime_providers_shared.dll
  cargo:rerun-if-changed=D:\GIT\scrfd\target\release\build\onnxruntime_providers_tensorrt.dll

  --- stderr
```


`-Zbuild-dir-new-layout` [was introduced in March 2026](https://blog.rust-lang.org/2026/03/13/call-for-testing-build-dir-layout-v2/) and Layout v2 is now the default for the latest nightly builds. I ran into this updating my Cargo toolchain from to the latest 1.100.0-nightly, after which I could no longer perform clean builds of my project depending on `ort` (with no other changes).

As a temporary workaround, setting the environment variable `__CARGO_TEMPORARY_BUILD_DIR_NEW_LAYOUT_OPT_OUT=1` forcibly disables Layout v2 and allows `ort-sys` build script to complete correctly.

items.title: CUDA EP: release_env_on_exit reads freed memory, aborting at exit — reproduces without a second CUDA library (cf. #564, #392, #169)

labels.name: stale
labels.description: No response received from author for a while

items.body:
## Summary

`release_env_on_exit` → `ReleaseEnv` reads freed memory inside
`libonnxruntime_providers_cuda.so`, aborting the process at exit with
`corrupted double-linked list` **after a completely successful, correct run**.

This is the same failure as #564, #392 and #169. #564 was closed on the theory
that `libtorch` and ONNX Runtime were clashing over CUDA ownership. I think that
conclusion was premature, and I have a repro that isolates it:

- **no second CUDA framework** — no torch, no TensorRT; the only consumer of the
  CUDA EP is `ort` itself;
- the probability **scales with how much CUDA EP work the process did**, which
  matches #392's "increase `num_sessions` to increase probability" (that reporter
  also had no second framework — TensorRT EP alone);
- a one-line workaround that prevents `ReleaseEnv` from running fixes it
  completely, which points squarely at the teardown rather than at any other
  library's destructors.

Results are never affected — every run wrote complete, byte-correct output. Only
the exit status is wrong, which is nonetheless fatal for us: a workflow engine
reads a non-zero exit as a failed job.

## Environment

- `ort` 2.0.0-rc.13, `load-dynamic`, `cuda`
- onnxruntime 1.27.1 (`onnxruntime-linux-x64-gpu_cuda13-1.27.1`)
- CUDA 13.0 driver 580.126.09, NVIDIA A30, Rust 1.9x, glibc 2.34, Rocky 9

## Measurement

Two binaries of the same application, interleaved, 10 runs each on identical
input, differing only in how much work goes through the CUDA EP:

| build | CUDA-EP sessions | non-zero exit | output complete |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | 1 small CNN (`[B,1,806] -> [B,2,806]`) | **0/10** | 10/10 |
| after | that CNN **plus** 2 LSTM encoder sessions (`[B,1,3000] -> [300,B,1280]`) | **5/10** | 10/10 |

Same machine, same input, same onnxruntime. The only change is more CUDA EP
state to unwind. Toggling everything else in our own code made no difference:
our GPU decode off, our zero-copy output binding off, one encoder session instead
of two — all still ~50%.

## Valgrind

On a run whose output was complete and correct (10 errors, 5 contexts, **all** at
teardown, none in the processing loop):

```
Invalid read of size 8
   at 0x10545A7C: ??? (in .../lib/libonnxruntime_providers_cuda.so)
   by 0xD158780: ??? (in .../lib/libonnxruntime.so.1.27.1)
   by 0xD159013: ??? (in .../lib/libonnxruntime.so.1.27.1)
   by 0xD132ECC: ??? (in .../lib/libonnxruntime.so.1.27.1)
   by 0xD132F9C: ??? (in .../lib/libonnxruntime.so.1.27.1)
   by 0xD10BC9C: ??? (in .../lib/libonnxruntime.so.1.27.1)
   by 0xB59C42: <alloc::sync::Arc<ort::environment::Environment>>::drop_slow (src/lib.rs:327)
   by 0xB59B6F: ort::environment::release_env_on_exit (library/alloc/src/sync.rs:2874)
   by 0x4006282: _dl_fini (dl-fini.c:148)
   by 0x49B9E7C: __run_exit_handlers
   by 0x49B9FCF: exit
Address 0x51f94ee8 is 1,258,744 bytes inside an unallocated block of size 1,360,656 in arena "client"
```

This is byte-for-byte the same shape as the trace @decahedron1 posted in #564 —
same provider library, same call chain, same "unallocated block". Reaching it
without `libtorch` in the process is the new information.

gdb on the abort itself (symbolized, `.fini_array` path):

```
#5  unlink_chunk.constprop ()
#6  malloc_consolidate ()
#7  _int_free ()
#8  free ()
#9-14  libonnxruntime.so.1.27.1
#15 ort::environment::{impl#5}::drop        ort-2.0.0-rc.13/src/lib.rs:327
#22 ort::environment::release_env_on_exit   environment.rs:85
#23 _dl_fini (dl-fini.c:148)
```

Also matching #564: the abort disappears under gdb and under valgrind — the
invalid *read* is still reported, but glibc never gets to the free that notices.

## Workaround that works

`release_env_on_exit` does `G_ENV.lock().take()`, which only runs `ReleaseEnv`
when the **last** `Arc<Environment>` drops — and every live `Session` holds one
through `SharedSessionInner::_environment`. Leaking the objects that own our
sessions keeps the count above zero, so the faulty path never executes:

```rust
// after all work is done and all output flushed
std::mem::forget(model);     // owns the encoder Sessions
std::mem::forget(detector);  // owns the CNN Session
```

Back to **0/10** over the same interleaved 10-run comparison, everything else
unchanged. That it works is itself evidence the problem is confined to
`ReleaseEnv` and not to some other library's destructor ordering.

`--features load-dynamic` is not optional for us: the CUDA-enabled
`libonnxruntime` is supplied at run time on machines that differ from the build
host, so the static-binary suggestion from #564 is not available.

## Suggestion

An explicit, supported way to opt out of the at-exit release would turn this from
a `mem::forget` trick into something documentable — roughly what @SephVelut
proposed at the end of #564. Either direction would do:

- `ort::init().with_release_env_on_exit(false)`, or
- an `ort::cleanup()` the application calls before `main` returns, with the
  `.fini_array` hook skipped if it has already run.

The second is nicer in principle but has the same hazard if it is called after
whatever is being freed has gone; the first is a blunt escape hatch that is at
least honest about what it does.

Happy to test a patch — I have a machine that reproduces this at ~50% and a
reduced case if that would help.

items.title: [Bug] CUDA 13 feature fails to load due to missing cublasLt64_12.dll, CUDA 12 works fine
items.body:
Environment
OS: Windows 11 x64
Rust version:  1.97.1 (8bab26f4f 2026-07-14)
ort crate version: 2.0.0-rc.12
Target: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
ONNX Runtime: bundled prebuilt binaries from ort

Problem Description
When building the project with cuda-13 feature enabled, the CUDA execution provider still tries to load CUDA 12 runtime library cublasLt64_12.dll and fails with module missing error.
If I switch to cuda-12 feature and provide matching CUDA 12 runtime DLLs, CUDA EP loads successfully without any error.

Full error log

PS F:\projects\rust\capture> cargo run --release -- --model yolo8n --conf 0.7
    Finished `release` profile [optimized] target(s) in 0.09s
     Running `target\release\capture.exe --model yolo8n --conf 0.7`
2026-07-18T10:30:43.471976Z  INFO capture: Capture source 2560x1380
2026-07-18T10:30:43.472492Z  INFO capture: Model: yolo8n  path=data/models/yolo8n.onnx  input=640  labels=80
2026-07-18T10:30:43.500030Z ERROR ort::ep: An error occurred when attempting to register `CUDAExecutionProvider`: D:\a\ort-artifacts\ort-artifacts\onnxruntime\onnxruntime\core\session\provider_bridge_ort.cc:1952 onnxruntime::ProviderLibrary::Get [ONNXRuntimeError] : 1 : FAIL : Error loading "F:\projects\rust\capture\target\release\onnxruntime_providers_cuda.dll" which depends on "cublasLt64_12.dll" which is missing.
